summary: Read-only design panel: three independent designs for ha-ros2-bridge, judged, synthesised, then adversarially checked

final.perspective: Finaliser pass over the synthesised design against the two objection sets. Every blocker and major objection is applied: HA-side command bookkeeping now persists session, deadline and source per command and reconciles after the retained replay burst instead of after a fixed 5 s, so an HA restart or options reload mid-task re-adopts the running task; the session filter on acks, feedback and results is removed (replies route by id alone, session is used only to detect a node restart); HA suspends the result deadline while the robot reports the task paused; command ids are validated as UUIDs and robot ids against the pattern before any topic is built, every publish is guarded and the inbound queue is bounded; duplicate robot ids are detected on both sides (0x8E takeover handling and an instance field) with a repair issue; the HA half is written against probatio (verified: voluptuous is not installed at 2026.10.1 and exists only as a sys.modules alias); intents are registered once and never removed; ament_copyright is dropped because it cannot read SPDX headers. All minor objections are applied too (Retain As Published on the cmd subscription, prefix validation and discarding the reserved ha segment, a persisted dedupe store, late-ack re-adoption and result-before-ack, cancel as ack-terminal with last_result tracking motion tasks only, Store writes before publish and age-bounded seen_results, publish_failed keeping the command pending, quality-scale corrections and async_entity_id_changed, a flake8 config handed to ament_flake8, the explicit one-shot timer pattern). One objection is applied only in part: refusing the configured MQTT discovery prefix would require reading mqtt internals, so the flow refuses the literal homeassistant plus wildcard and slash forms instead (recorded in risks). Decisions only Jonny can make remain dated single questions.
final.design_summary: ha-ros2-bridge is one Apache-2.0 monorepo with a written MQTT contract (JSON schemas, golden and must-reject examples, HMAC vectors) consumed by two halves. The ROS 2 side is an ament_python package, one rclpy process per robot: a paho-mqtt 2.1.0 network thread hands inbound messages to a SingleThreadedExecutor through a bounded deque and a GuardCondition, where rclpy-free modules authorise commands (size, UUID id, schema, robot id, topic-bound HMAC, persisted dedupe, freshness, allowlist, params, state gating), drive a TaskExecutor plugin (fake executor shipped), publish retained announce, state and availability (LWT), a 2 s heartbeat, and per-task retained acks and results with MQTT 5 expiry. The HA side is a thin probatio-validated custom integration riding HA's own MQTT connection: one device per announced robot with state, last-result and problem sensors, a task-result event entity and one button per parameterless task plus cancel; services send_task, cancel_task, get_robots; three bus events; two Assist intents; diagnostics and five repair issues. Every command id ends in exactly one named outcome, re-adopted across HA restarts and synthesised only when the robot truly never answers. HA is advisory, ROS owns safety, the watchdog defaults to informational.

final.mqtt_contract:
## Conventions

- `{prefix}` defaults to `ros2_bridge` (no leading or trailing slash, no `+` or `#`, not `homeassistant`). `{robot_id}` and task names match `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}$`; `ha` is reserved and refused as a robot id. Command ids (`{task_id}`) are UUID4 strings matching `^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-4[0-9a-f]{3}-[89ab][0-9a-f]{3}-[0-9a-f]{12}$`. Both halves validate the topic segment and the payload field against these patterns before any registry, topic or publish use; anything else is dropped and counted, never answered.
- Every JSON payload is a UTF-8 object carrying `"schema": 1`. Receivers ignore unknown fields; schema 1 only gains optional fields. Timestamps are integer epoch milliseconds UTC.
- Size limits: 16 KiB per message, 64 KiB for announce; larger payloads are dropped unparsed and counted.
- MQTT 5 on both sides. ROS connects with `clean_start=True`; broker-queued copies of commands are therefore never drained after a restart, and publisher-side QoS 1 retransmissions are caught by the persisted dedupe store (see failure table). Commands are never retained; replies are retained with Message Expiry Interval (ack 120 s, result 300 s, both parameters).
- `instance` is `"<hostname>:<pid>"` of the publishing node process, carried in announce, state and heartbeat so two nodes claiming one robot id are visible.

## Topic table

| Topic | Direction | QoS | Retain | Expiry | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `{prefix}/{robot_id}/announce` | ROS to HA | 1 | yes | none | Identity plus task catalogue. Empty retained payload is a tombstone. Republished on connect, on `homeassistant/status` `online` after 0 to `announce.jitter_s`, and on catalogue change. |
| `{prefix}/{robot_id}/availability` | ROS to HA | 1 | yes | none | `online` on connect, `offline` as LWT and on clean shutdown. |
| `{prefix}/{robot_id}/state` | ROS to HA | 1 | yes | none | On change and on (re)connect. |
| `{prefix}/{robot_id}/heartbeat` | ROS to HA | 0 | no | 5 s | Every `heartbeat.interval_s` (2; 0 disables and HA then does no staleness tracking). |
| `{prefix}/{robot_id}/cmd` | HA to ROS | 1 | never | `ceil(max_age_ms/1000)` | Node subscribes with `SubscribeOptions(qos=1, retainAsPublished=True)`, so a planted retained copy is seen with RETAIN 1 both live and at reconnect, dropped, counted and cleared with an empty retained publish; the node's own clearing echo (empty payload) is ignored silently. |
| `{prefix}/{robot_id}/task/{task_id}/ack` | ROS to HA | 1 | yes | `reply.ack_expiry_s` (120) | One distinct ack per id; a duplicate command republishes the stored ack bytes. |
| `{prefix}/{robot_id}/task/{task_id}/feedback` | ROS to HA | 0 | no | 10 s | Optional, throttled to `reply.feedback_max_rate_hz` (2). |
| `{prefix}/{robot_id}/task/{task_id}/result` | ROS to HA | 1 | yes | `reply.result_expiry_s` (300) | Exactly one per accepted task command. Cancel commands have no result (ack-terminal). |
| `{prefix}/ha/heartbeat` | HA to ROS | 0 | no | 5 s | Every `heartbeat_interval_s` (2; 0 disables). Not published while HA's MQTT client is disconnected. HA's own `+/heartbeat` handler discards the `ha` segment. |
| `{prefix}/ha/sensors/{domain}/{object_id}` | HA to ROS | 0 | yes | none | Canonical republish of `mirror_entities`; cleared when an entity leaves the option, when the prefix changes, and on entry removal. |
| `homeassistant/status` | HA birth and will | 0 | no | none | Node re-announces on `online`. |
| `zigbee2mqtt/{name}` and `/availability` | Zigbee2MQTT | as published | as configured | none | Fast path, mirrored unchanged with source availability. |

HA subscribes once at setup to `{prefix}/+/announce`, `+/availability`, `+/state`, `+/heartbeat`, `+/task/+/ack`, `+/task/+/result` (QoS 1) and `+/task/+/feedback` (QoS 0); every wildcard handler first checks the robot segment against the pattern and discards `ha`. `async_on_subscribe_done` on the ack and result filters gates `hub.ready` (bounded 10 s). The node subscribes to `cmd` (QoS 1, Retain As Published), `ha/heartbeat`, `homeassistant/status`, each `mirror.topics` entry and its availability sibling (QoS 0).

## announce

```json
{"schema": 1, "robot_id": "arm_left", "name": "Left arm", "manufacturer": "Example Robotics", "model": "UR3e",
 "sw_version": "driver 2.4.1", "hw_version": null, "serial_number": null, "suggested_area": "Kitchen",
 "bridge_version": "0.1.0", "executor": {"name": "fake", "version": "0.1.0"},
 "session": "9f1c7a0e-4a1b-4b2c-8d1e-0f1a2b3c4d5e", "instance": "robotpc:4123",
 "capabilities": {"cancel": true, "feedback": true, "hmac_required": false},
 "watchdog_mode": "none", "heartbeat_interval_s": 2,
 "tasks": [
  {"name": "reset", "label": "Reset to home", "kind": "motion", "timeout_s": 60, "params": null},
  {"name": "stop", "label": "Stop", "kind": "control", "timeout_s": 5, "params": null},
  {"name": "pause", "label": "Pause", "kind": "control", "timeout_s": 5, "params": null},
  {"name": "resume", "label": "Resume", "kind": "control", "timeout_s": 5, "params": null},
  {"name": "move_to", "label": "Move to named pose", "kind": "motion", "timeout_s": 120,
   "params": {"type": "object", "properties": {"pose": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["pose"]}}],
 "ts": 1760356800000}
```

- `tasks` is the allowlist after the operator's `tasks.allow` intersection; a task with no required params gets a button; every task is callable through `send_task`. `kind`: `motion` (rejected while busy, in error or inhibited; owns the single active slot), `control` (any state: stop, pause, resume), `query` (any state, no motion).
- `params` is a JSON Schema subset: `type: object`, `properties` with `type` in {string, number, integer, boolean}, optional `enum`, `minimum`, `maximum`, plus `required`; validated by hand-written code on both sides.
- `session` is a new UUID4 per node process. HA uses it only to detect a node restart (reconciliation below); it never filters replies.

## availability: plain `online` or `offline`.

## state

```json
{"schema": 1, "robot_id": "arm_left", "state": "busy",
 "task_id": "6a0c2b58-1d7e-4a1f-9b2a-3c4d5e6f7a8b", "task": "move_to", "since": 1760356801000,
 "paused": false, "inhibited": false, "ha_link": "up", "watchdog_mode": "none",
 "executor_health": {"level": "ok", "message": ""}, "error": null,
 "session": "9f1c...", "instance": "robotpc:4123", "seq": 42, "ts": 1760356801003}
```

- `state` is exactly `idle`, `busy` or `error` (Q17); `paused`, `inhibited`, `ha_link` are separate fields. `error` is null or `{"code", "reason"}`. A failed task alone never sets `error`.
- `seq` increments per publication within a session; HA drops a state whose `seq` regresses within the same session. HA uses `task_id` plus `paused` to suspend and resume its own result deadline for that command.

## heartbeat (ROS to HA)

```json
{"schema": 1, "robot_id": "arm_left", "session": "9f1c...", "instance": "robotpc:4123", "seq": 1203,
 "ts": 1760356804000, "uptime_s": 2406, "ha_clock_offset_ms": 12,
 "counters": {"accepted": 12, "rejected": 1, "duplicates": 0, "dropped_retained": 0, "dropped_oversize": 0,
              "dropped_invalid_id": 0, "dropped_queue_full": 0, "publish_errors": 0, "takeovers": 0}}
```

## heartbeat (HA to ROS)

```json
{"schema": 1, "ts": 1760356800000, "seq": 1234, "interval_ms": 2000, "instance_id": "c2a4..."}
```

## cmd (task)

```json
{"schema": 1, "id": "6a0c2b58-1d7e-4a1f-9b2a-3c4d5e6f7a8b", "type": "task", "robot_id": "arm_left",
 "task": "move_to", "params": {"pose": "home"}, "issued_at": 1760356800950, "max_age_ms": 5000, "timeout_s": null,
 "source": {"origin": "ha", "instance_id": "c2a4...", "kind": "intent", "user_id": "a1b2c3",
            "context_id": "01J9ZX...", "device_id": "voice_pe_kitchen_device_id"},
 "sig": "3f1a...64 hex (only when a secret is configured)"}
```

## cmd (cancel)

```json
{"schema": 1, "id": "0c1d...", "type": "cancel", "robot_id": "arm_left", "target_id": null,
 "issued_at": 1760356802000, "max_age_ms": 5000,
 "source": {"origin": "ha", "instance_id": "c2a4...", "kind": "button", "user_id": null, "context_id": "01J9ZY...", "device_id": null}}
```

- `id` is a UUID4 generated by HA and names the reply topics; `robot_id` must equal the topic segment. `target_id` null means the active motion task. `timeout_s` null means the announced value; a value is clamped to `command.task_timeout_cap_s`.
- HMAC: `sig = hex(HMAC-SHA256(secret, topic + "\n" + canonical))`, `canonical = json.dumps(payload_without_sig, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False).encode()`; constant-time compare; vectors in `contract/hmac_vectors.json`.
- Freshness: accept when `-skew <= now - issued_at <= min(max_age_ms, command.max_age_cap_ms) + skew`, `skew = command.clock_skew_tolerance_ms` (2000); otherwise `rejected_stale` or `rejected_future` with the measured skew.

## ack

```json
{"schema": 1, "id": "6a0c...", "robot_id": "arm_left", "type": "task", "task": "move_to",
 "accepted": false, "code": "rejected_busy", "reason": "Task 'reset' (id 51f0...) is running",
 "received_at": 1760356800962, "clock_skew_ms": 12, "session": "9f1c...", "ts": 1760356800963}
```

Codes (closed set): `accepted`, `rejected_malformed`, `rejected_unknown_task`, `rejected_invalid_params`, `rejected_stale`, `rejected_future`, `rejected_unauthorised`, `rejected_busy`, `rejected_error`, `rejected_inhibited`, `rejected_executor`, `rejected_no_such_task`. A repeated id republishes the stored ack. A command whose `id` is not a UUID gets no ack (there is no safe topic to publish to) and is counted as `dropped_invalid_id`. For `type: cancel`, `accepted` is the terminal outcome of that command id; the cancelled task's own result follows under its own id.

## feedback

```json
{"schema": 1, "id": "6a0c...", "robot_id": "arm_left", "progress": 0.4, "stage": "executing",
 "message": "waypoint 2 of 5", "session": "9f1c...", "ts": 1760356802100}
```

## result

```json
{"schema": 1, "id": "6a0c...", "robot_id": "arm_left", "task": "move_to", "kind": "motion",
 "status": "aborted", "goal_status": 6, "code": "collision", "reason": "Planned path collides with object 'mug_42'",
 "data": {"moveit_error_code": -12}, "started_at": 1760356800970, "finished_at": 1760356803410,
 "session": "9f1c...", "ts": 1760356803412}
```

- `status` maps onto `action_msgs/GoalStatus`: `succeeded` 4, `cancelled` 5, `aborted` 6. `kind` repeats the task kind so HA can route control results away from `last_result`.
- `code` is `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$`; recommended vocabulary: `ok`, `cancelled`, `preempted`, `collision`, `self_collision`, `no_trajectory`, `planning_failed`, `control_failed`, `timeout`, `invalid_goal`, `controller_error`, `inhibited`, `executor_error`, `executor_unresponsive`, `nothing_to_pause`, `unknown`.
- HA-synthesised codes never travel on the wire: `no_ack`, `no_result`, `node_restarted`, `ha_restarted`.

## sensors (canonical path, HA to ROS)

Topic `{prefix}/ha/sensors/binary_sensor/kitchen_motion`:

```json
{"schema": 1, "entity_id": "binary_sensor.kitchen_motion", "domain": "binary_sensor", "object_id": "kitchen_motion",
 "state": "on", "available": true, "device_class": "motion", "unit": null,
 "attributes": {"friendly_name": "Kitchen motion"}, "last_changed": "2026-10-13T12:00:00.123456+00:00", "ts": 1760356800123}
```

Retained QoS 0 on every state change and once at setup; `unavailable` and `unknown` become `state: null, available: false`; attributes filtered to the documented allowlist.

## Reply routing and reconciliation rules (HA side)

- Replies (`ack`, `feedback`, `result`) are matched by `id` alone. The `session` field is informational.
- `ack` (live or retained): resolves the pending command if present. A late `accepted` ack for a command already in `timeout_no_ack` re-opens it as `running` and fires `ros2_bridge_task_ack` with `late: true`; a late rejected ack leaves it terminal. Retained acks never fire events except in that re-open case.
- `result`: if `id` is in `seen_results`, ignore; otherwise fire `ros2_bridge_task_result` once (`replayed: true` for retained deliveries), update entities, record `(id, finished_at)`. A result may terminate a command in `sent` (no ack seen yet) as well as in `running`.
- Reconciliation runs once per hub start, after `hub.ready` and `mqtt_connected` are both true plus a `replay_settle_s` (3) quiet period, and again whenever a robot's `session` changes (after a 1 s grace). Per outstanding command: result already seen, nothing to do; robot's current session equals the stored session and the deadline has not passed, re-adopt as `running` and re-arm the remaining deadline (suspended if the retained state shows it paused); session differs, `lost` (`node_restarted`); deadline passed, `timeout` (`no_result`); robot never announced within `replay_settle_s`, wait for its announce or the deadline, whichever first.

## Failure behaviour (full table with test ids in docs/failure-modes.md)

| Failure | Mechanism | What HA shows |
|---|---|---|
| Broker restart | Retained announce, state, availability republished on reconnect; QoS 1 replies queued by paho | Robots unavailable while HA's MQTT is down, then recover; in-flight commands resolve from retained replies or re-adoption |
| HA restart or options reload mid-task | Store carries session and deadline; reconciliation after the replay burst | Running task re-adopted; its real result fires as `task_result`, never `late_result` |
| ROS node restart | New `session`; stored session per command | Non-terminal commands for that robot become `lost` after 1 s grace unless a result arrived |
| Node connected but hung | Heartbeat stops while keepalive continues | `problem` on (`heartbeat_stale`); entities unavailable after `heartbeat_unavailable_after_s` (30) |
| Dead node, broker down at the moment of death (no LWT) | Same staleness rule | Unavailable after the same timer despite retained `online` |
| QoS 1 redelivery, same process | Dedupe store republishes the stored ack | Nothing new |
| Publisher-side QoS 1 resend across a node restart | Dedupe store persisted to disk, reloaded for ids younger than `max_age_cap_ms + skew` | Nothing new; one `executor.start` |
| Planted retained command | Retain As Published subscription, drop, count, clear | `dropped_retained` in diagnostics |
| Command with non-UUID or wildcard id | Dropped before any topic is built | `dropped_invalid_id` counter |
| Stale or skewed command | Freshness window | `rejected_stale` or `rejected_future`; `clock_skew` repair |
| Lost ack | Ack retained 120 s; late accepted ack re-opens | `timeout` (`no_ack`, documented as outcome unknown) until a late ack arrives |
| Result before ack (per-topic ordering only) | `sent` to terminal transition | Result applied normally |
| Pause longer than margin | HA suspends the result deadline while state shows the task paused | No spurious timeout |
| Publish fails (HA's client disconnected) | paho keeps the QoS 1 message and resends on reconnect; command stays `sent` | `publish_failed` raised to the caller; outcome still tracked |
| Two nodes, one robot id, same client id | Broker DISCONNECT 0x8E; node logs ERROR, backs off, exits after `mqtt.takeover_exit_after`; HA counts session flaps | `duplicate_robot_id` repair |
| Two nodes, one robot id, distinct client ids | Differing `instance` within one heartbeat interval | `duplicate_robot_id` repair |
| Executor never finishes | Task timeout, cancel, grace, forced `aborted/timeout` or `executor_unresponsive` | `last_result` aborted, robot `error`, `problem` on |
| Misfiring automation | Rejected acks beyond `reply.retained_rejections_per_minute` published non-retained; `max_pending_per_robot` | `too_many_pending` |

## Shape

One executable `bridge_node`, one process per robot. `BridgeNode(rclpy.node.Node)` is wiring only; `protocol.py`, `authoriser.py`, `task_manager.py`, `dedupe_store.py`, `watchdog.py`, `sensor_mirror.py`, `executors/base.py`, `executors/fake.py` import neither rclpy nor paho and are unit-tested on any machine.

## Threading model

```
paho network thread (loop_start)                   rclpy SingleThreadedExecutor (main thread)
 on_message: size check, append to deque(maxlen)   GuardCondition callback drains the deque:
   (topic, payload, retain, rx_ts), guard.trigger()  cmd -> Authoriser -> TaskManager -> executor.start/cancel
   full deque: drop, count dropped_queue_full        heartbeat -> Watchdog; ha status -> re-announce after jitter
 on_connect / on_disconnect: append event, trigger   mirror -> SensorMirror -> ~/mqtt_in
 MqttLink.publish() called only from the main        timers: watchdog tick 0.5 s, health poll 1 s, heartbeat 2 s,
   thread; every call wrapped in try/except          per-task timeout and cancel grace (self-cancelling timers)
   (ValueError, OSError): ERROR log, publish_errors  TaskHandle.finish/feedback from a plugin thread -> ctx.post -> deque
```

- Guard-condition triggering from the paho thread is safe (rcl documents it). All robot state lives on the main thread; plugin methods run there too. Plugin calls are timed: longer than `executor.call_warn_s` (0.1) logs WARN and marks `executor_health` degraded; a call that blocks for ever stalls this robot only, the heartbeat stops and HA shows `problem`. No thread-pool guard (recorded decision, unchanged).
- rclpy Jazzy has no one-shot timer (verified): every one-shot (task timeout, cancel grace, fake task completion, announce jitter) is a periodic timer that calls `timer.cancel()` as the first line of its callback; pause uses `timer.cancel()` with the remaining period stored, resume creates a fresh timer for the remainder. The pattern is stated once in `task_manager.py` and in `writing-an-executor.md`.
- No publish is allowed to end the process: `MqttLink.publish` validates the topic against the contract patterns first (so a wildcard or over-long topic is impossible by construction), then catches `ValueError` and `OSError` from paho, logs at ERROR with the topic, increments `publish_errors` and returns False.

## Executor plugin interface (`executors/base.py`)

```python
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any, Callable, Literal, Mapping, Protocol, Sequence

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TaskSpec:
    name: str; label: str
    kind: Literal["motion", "control", "query"] = "motion"
    timeout_s: float = 60.0
    params: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    description: str = ""

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TaskRequest:
    id: str; task: str; params: Mapping[str, Any]; issued_at: int; timeout_s: float; source: Mapping[str, Any]

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TaskResult:
    status: Literal["succeeded", "cancelled", "aborted"]
    code: str; reason: str = ""; data: Mapping[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    @property
    def goal_status(self) -> int: return {"succeeded": 4, "cancelled": 5, "aborted": 6}[self.status]

class TaskRejected(Exception):
    def __init__(self, code: str = "rejected_executor", reason: str = "") -> None: ...

class TaskHandle(Protocol):
    """One per task. Thread-safe. Calls after the terminal finish are logged and ignored."""
    task_id: str
    def feedback(self, progress: float | None = None, stage: str = "", message: str = "") -> None: ...
    def finish(self, result: TaskResult) -> None: ...

class BridgeContext:
    """Given to the executor in setup(). Every method is thread-safe."""
    node: "rclpy.node.Node"; logger: "RcutilsLogger"; robot_id: str
    def post(self, fn: Callable[[], None]) -> None: ...
    def set_error(self, code: str, reason: str) -> None: ...
    def clear_error(self) -> None: ...
    def set_paused(self, paused: bool) -> None: ...   # state.paused; pauses the task timeout clock
    def ha_link_ok(self) -> bool: ...

class TaskExecutor(ABC):
    name: str = "base"; version: str = "0.0.0"
    @abstractmethod
    def setup(self, ctx: BridgeContext) -> None: ...          # blocking waits allowed here only
    @abstractmethod
    def tasks(self) -> Sequence[TaskSpec]: ...
    @abstractmethod
    def start(self, req: TaskRequest, handle: TaskHandle) -> None: ...   # return promptly; raise TaskRejected to refuse
    @abstractmethod
    def cancel(self, task_id: str) -> None: ...               # must lead to finish(cancelled) within cancel_grace_s
    def stop_and_hold(self, reason: str) -> None: ...
    def health(self) -> tuple[Literal["ok", "degraded", "error"], str]: return ("ok", "")
    def shutdown(self) -> None: ...
```

Loading: a colon means `importlib.import_module` plus `getattr`; otherwise `importlib.metadata.entry_points(group="ros2_ha_bridge.executors")`. Unknown or wrong type is a fatal startup error.

## Fake executor

Tasks `reset`, `move_to {pose}`, `wait {seconds}` (cancellable, feedback), `fail {code: enum of the MoveIt failure classes}`, `hang` (timeout 10 s), `raise_error`, `clear_error`, and the Q7 set `stop` (cancels the active task, `cancelled/preempted`), `pause` (`ctx.set_paused(True)`, own result `succeeded` or `aborted/nothing_to_pause`), `resume`. Deterministic with an injected clock.

## Action lifecycle mapping (documented with a MoveIt 2 sketch)

`send_goal_async` inside `start()` (returns at once; ack accepted follows); goal not accepted later gives `finish(aborted, invalid_goal)`; feedback callback to `handle.feedback`; `get_result_async` done maps GoalStatus 4, 5, 6; `cancel_goal_async` from `cancel()`.

## Command handling (main thread; first failure wins)

0. Delivery with RETAIN set on `cmd` (possible live because of Retain As Published): empty payload from our own clear is ignored; otherwise drop, WARN, `dropped_retained`, publish empty retained to clear. No ack.
1. Oversize: drop, count. No ack.
2. JSON parse; `id` must be a string matching the UUID pattern, else drop, `dropped_invalid_id`, rate-limited WARN. No ack. Everything after this point has a safe reply topic.
3. `schema == 1`, required fields typed, else `rejected_malformed`.
4. Payload `robot_id` equals this node's id (the topic segment is ours by subscription), else `rejected_malformed`.
5. HMAC when a secret is configured, else `rejected_unauthorised` (rate-limited WARN).
6. Dedupe (persisted store): known id republishes the stored ack bytes, retained, same expiry, and stops. Runs before freshness so a redelivery can never downgrade an `accepted` ack.
7. Freshness: `rejected_stale` or `rejected_future` with `clock_skew_ms`.
8. `type == "task"`: allowlist (`rejected_unknown_task`), params subset (`rejected_invalid_params`), `timeout_s` clamp.
9. State gating by kind: `motion` refused while busy, error or inhibited; `control` and `query` pass.
10. `executor.start`: `TaskRejected` to `rejected_executor`; other exceptions to `rejected_executor` with one traceback. Success: ack accepted, dedupe store write (memory and file), `busy` plus `state` for motion, timer armed.
11. `type == "cancel"`: steps 0 to 7, resolve `target_id`; unknown gives `rejected_no_such_task`; otherwise ack accepted (terminal for the cancel id) and `executor.cancel(target)`.

Finish path, forced finishes, `health()` handling, pause semantics and the rejected-ack rate limit are as before: `handle.finish()` publishes the retained result with `kind`, returns to `idle` for motion; task timeout gives `cancel()` then after `cancel_grace_s` a forced `aborted/timeout`, or `executor_unresponsive` if cancel produced nothing, with the robot in `error` until cleared; paused tasks stay `busy` with `paused: true` and a frozen clock.

## Dedupe store (`dedupe_store.py`)

Ordered dict of `id -> (received_at, ack_bytes)` bounded by `command.dedupe_size` and `command.dedupe_window_s`. On accept and on every rejection ack the entry is written to memory; accepted entries are appended to `data_dir/dedupe.json` (rewritten atomically, at most once per second, oldest entries pruned). At start the file is loaded and only ids younger than `command.max_age_cap_ms + command.clock_skew_tolerance_ms` are kept, which is exactly the window in which a publisher-side QoS 1 resend could still pass the freshness check.

## Watchdog

0.5 s timer; `none`, `inhibit_new`, `stop_and_hold` as recorded (Q16); `~/ha_link` latched Bool; HA heartbeat `ts` feeds `ha_clock_offset_ms`.

## Connection lifecycle

1. Startup: parameters, env secrets, `robot.id` validation, `load_executor`, `setup`, announce computed, dedupe file loaded.
2. `MqttLink`: `Client(CallbackAPIVersion.VERSION2, client_id, protocol=MQTTv5, reconnect_on_failure=True)`, `username_pw_set`, optional `tls_set`, `will_set(availability, "offline", qos=1, retain=True)`, `reconnect_delay_set`, `connect_async(..., clean_start=True)`, `loop_start()`.
3. `on_connect` failure codes logged once each in plain language; success subscribes (`cmd` with `SubscribeOptions(qos=1, retainAsPublished=True)`, the rest plain QoS 0) and posts `connected`, which publishes `availability online`, `announce`, `state`.
4. `on_disconnect` with reason code 142 (`Session taken over`): ERROR naming the robot id and the likely cause (another node with the same `robot.id`), `takeovers` counter, reconnect delay doubled per takeover; after `mqtt.takeover_exit_after` takeovers in 10 minutes the node exits non-zero so launch `respawn_max_retries` (3) stops the flapping.
5. HA birth `online`: re-announce after jitter.
6. Clean shutdown: stop inbound, publish `availability offline` with `wait_for_publish(2.0)`, `disconnect()`, `loop_stop()`, `executor.shutdown()`, flush the dedupe file, destroy the node.

## Sensor mirror and ROS interfaces

Unchanged: `std_msgs/String` envelope on `~/mqtt_in` with `source_available`; `~/ha_link` latched Bool. No custom message package.

## Launch, packaging and lint

`bridge.launch.py` and `fleet.launch.py` as before, with `respawn=True, respawn_delay=2.0, respawn_max_retries=3`. `package.xml` format 3, Apache-2.0, `exec_depend` rclpy std_msgs action_msgs launch launch_ros ros2launch; `test_depend` ament_flake8, ament_pep257, python3-pytest. ament_copyright is not used: it has no SPDX support and requires a `Copyright YYYY Holder` line followed by the full Apache notice (verified), which contradicts the Q18 decision to use SPDX headers; `scripts/check_spdx.py` runs over `ros2/` in `ros2.yml` and pre-commit instead (recorded in docs/decisions.md). `test/test_flake8.py` calls `main_with_errors(argv=["--config", <package>/.flake8])` (the `--config` argument is verified); that file keeps ament's extend-ignore list and max-line-length 99 and adds `Q000,I100,I101,I201,I202` because ruff (quote-style single, line-length 99 for `ros2/`) owns formatting and import order. paho comes from pip (`requirements.txt`), version checked at import. `setup.py` and `setup.cfg` as before.
final.ha_integration_design:
## Form

A thin MQTT-only custom integration (`dependencies: ["mqtt"]`, tasmota pattern) using `homeassistant.components.mqtt` helpers `async_publish`, `async_subscribe`, `async_on_subscribe_done`, `async_subscribe_connection_status`, `async_wait_for_mqtt_client`, `is_connected`, `mqtt_config_entry_enabled`, `valid_publish_topic`, `valid_subscribe_topic` (all exported at 2026.10.1). Every publish passes explicit `qos` and `retain` and `message_expiry_interval` where the contract says so. No pip requirements.

Validation uses `probatio` directly (`import probatio`), never `import voluptuous`: at 2026.10.1 core pins `probatio==0.13.0`, voluptuous is not installed and only exists as a `sys.modules` alias created at startup, core bans the voluptuous import, and `homeassistant.helpers.typing` defines `VolSchemaType = probatio.Schema | probatio.All | probatio.Any` and `VolDictType` (all verified). Service and slot schemas are annotated with those types; `cv.string`, `cv.ensure_list` and the other config_validation helpers are used where convenient (they are probatio-backed), with `probatio.AtLeastOne` in place of `cv.has_at_least_one_key` to match core's own lint rules. Tests assert on translation keys, not on validation error text, because probatio's wording differs from voluptuous. The migration is recorded in docs/upgrading.md, docs/decisions.md and docs/research/.

## manifest.json and hacs.json

```json
{"domain": "ros2_bridge", "name": "ROS 2 Bridge", "version": "0.1.0", "codeowners": ["@<jonny-github-handle>"],
 "config_flow": true, "dependencies": ["mqtt"], "mqtt": ["ros2_bridge/+/announce"],
 "documentation": "https://github.com/<owner>/ha-ros2-bridge/blob/main/docs/install-ha.md",
 "issue_tracker": "https://github.com/<owner>/ha-ros2-bridge/issues",
 "integration_type": "hub", "iot_class": "local_push", "requirements": [], "single_config_entry": true}
```

No `quality_scale` key. `hacs.json` `{"name": "ROS 2 Bridge", "homeassistant": "2026.10.0"}` with `brand/icon.png`. manifest.json has no licence key, so Q18's literal wording cannot be met there (one-line correction for Jonny at phase 0).

## Config flow (`VERSION = 1`, `MINOR_VERSION = 1`, `async_migrate_entry` stub)

- `async_step_user`: abort `mqtt_not_configured` unless `mqtt_config_entry_enabled`; abort `mqtt_not_available` unless `await async_wait_for_mqtt_client(hass)`; form with `topic_prefix` (default `ros2_bridge`) and optional `shared_secret` (password selector). Prefix validation (`_validate_prefix`): `valid_publish_topic(prefix)` (rejects `+` and `#`), no leading or trailing `/`, not empty, not `homeassistant` (the default discovery prefix; the configured one is not read because that needs mqtt internals), not `ha` as the first segment; error `invalid_prefix`. Unique id `DOMAIN`, `_abort_if_unique_id_configured`, `async_create_entry(title="ROS 2 Bridge", data={"instance_id": uuid4}, options={...})`.
- `async_step_mqtt(discovery_info: MqttServiceInfo)`: abort `single_instance_allowed` if an entry or flow exists; prefix from `subscribed_topic` minus `/+/announce`; abort `invalid_discovery_info` unless the payload decodes as a schema-1 announce with a valid robot id; then `async_step_confirm` ("Found robot {robot_name}. Create the ROS 2 Bridge entry?") with the optional secret.
- Options: `OptionsFlowWithReload`; fields `topic_prefix` (same validation), `shared_secret`, `heartbeat_interval_s` (0 to 10, default 2), `ack_timeout_s` (0.5 to 10, default 2.0), `command_max_age_ms` (1000 to 30000, default 5000), `result_timeout_margin_s` (default 10), `max_pending_per_robot` (default 16), `heartbeat_unavailable_after_s` (0 to 600, default 30, 0 disables), `mirror_entities` (entity selector, multiple).
- Inherited from `mqtt`, never asked: broker host, port, credentials, TLS, protocol version, birth and will.

## Setup and runtime model (push hub, no coordinator)

`async_setup` (runs once per HA start): registers the three services and the two intent handlers, and creates `hass.data[DOMAIN] = {"registries": {}}`, a container that outlives entry reloads. Handlers raise `HomeAssistantError(translation_key="not_loaded")` (services) or return an error response with the speech "The robot bridge is not loaded" (intents) when no hub is loaded. Intent handlers are never removed; `async_unload_entry` does not touch them (verified: `intent.async_remove` pops the handler globally, which would silence voice after the first options save).

`async_setup_entry`:
1. `if not await mqtt.async_wait_for_mqtt_client(hass): raise ConfigEntryNotReady`.
2. `CommandRegistry` is taken from `hass.data[DOMAIN]["registries"][entry.entry_id]` if an unload left it there (options reload), otherwise created and loaded from the Store.
3. `BridgeHub`, `entry.runtime_data = hub`.
4. `hub.async_start()`: seven subscriptions with sync `@callback` handlers (unsubscribe via `entry.async_on_unload`), `async_on_subscribe_done` on ack and result sets `hub.ready` (bounded 10 s), `async_subscribe_connection_status` drives `hub.mqtt_connected` (entities unavailable and heartbeat suppressed while False).
5. Forward platforms SENSOR, BINARY_SENSOR, BUTTON, EVENT.
6. HA heartbeat timer (`qos=0, retain=False, message_expiry_interval=5`) when the interval is above 0 and connected.
7. Housekeeping timer (1 s): ack and result deadlines (respecting pause suspension), robot heartbeat staleness and the unavailability timer, session grace expiry, reconciliation trigger.
8. Sensor mirror: `async_track_state_change_event` over `mirror_entities`; each published once; any topic recorded in the Store's `published_sensor_topics` that is no longer produced (entity removed from the option, or prefix changed) is cleared with an empty retained publish and dropped from the list.
9. Reconciliation: once `hub.ready` and `hub.mqtt_connected` have both been true for `replay_settle_s` (3 s constant), apply the contract's reconciliation rule to every outstanding command; commands for robots that have not announced yet wait for the announce or their deadline.

`async_unload_entry`: unload platforms, cancel timers, flush the Store, park the `CommandRegistry` in `hass.data` (pending futures from `wait: ack` or `wait: result` callers are resolved as cancelled, but the commands themselves stay outstanding and are reconciled by the next setup), subscriptions torn down by `async_on_unload`. `async_remove_entry`: clear every topic in `published_sensor_topics`, remove the parked registry, `store.async_remove()`.

## Store (`ros2_bridge.commands`, version 1)

```json
{"outstanding": {"<task_id>": {"robot_id": "arm_left", "task": "move_to", "kind": "motion", "type": "task",
                               "session": "9f1c...", "sent_at": 1760356800950, "deadline": 1760356930950,
                               "paused_at": null, "state": "running", "source": {...}}},
 "seen_results": [["<task_id>", 1760356803410], ...],
 "published_sensor_topics": ["ros2_bridge/ha/sensors/binary_sensor/kitchen_motion"]}
```

`await store.async_save()` runs before a command is published and on every terminal transition; the debounced `async_delay_save` is used only for feedback-free housekeeping (seen_results pruning). `session` is filled from the robot's current session at send time and updated from the accepted ack. `seen_results` is bounded by age (`reply.result_expiry_s` as announced, default 300 s, plus `result_timeout_margin_s`), not by count. A robot announcing `heartbeat_interval_s` 0 gets no staleness tracking.

## Message handling in the hub (every handler wrapped; a bad payload never kills a subscription callback)

- Topic segment check first: discard `ha` and anything not matching the robot id pattern, silently for `ha`, with a once-per-topic DEBUG otherwise.
- `availability`: `online` or `offline`; WARNING once when a robot goes offline, INFO when it returns.
- `announce`: decode (failure opens `invalid_announce`); empty payload is a tombstone (idempotent: a second tombstone for an unknown robot is a no-op); create or update the device (`identifiers={(DOMAIN, robot_id)}`), diff tasks, dispatch `robot_added` or `robot_updated`. A changed `session` starts the 1 s grace then reconciliation for that robot. An `instance` differing from the one seen within the last heartbeat interval, or more than 3 session changes in 5 minutes, opens `duplicate_robot_id` (closes after 10 quiet minutes).
- `state`: drop on `seq` regression within a session; dispatch `robot_updated`; pause tracking: when `task_id` matches an outstanding command and `paused` is true, record `paused_at` and stop its deadline; when `paused` returns to false or `task_id` changes, add the paused duration to the deadline and resume.
- `heartbeat` (ROS to HA): `last_heartbeat`, counters, `ha_clock_offset_ms`, `instance`.
- `ack`: by id; `accepted` moves `sent` to `running` and fires `ros2_bridge_task_ack`; `accepted: false` is terminal `rejected` (event entity type `rejected`); a late `accepted` ack re-opens `timeout_no_ack` to `running` and fires `task_ack` with `late: true`; for `type: cancel` an `accepted` ack is terminal `done` with no result expected. `clock_skew_ms` feeds the `clock_skew` repair; `rejected_unauthorised` with a secret configured, or `hmac_required` without one, opens `hmac_rejected`.
- `feedback`: state sensor attributes, at most one write per 500 ms per robot.
- `result`: by id, retained-replay rule; terminates a command in `sent` or `running`; after a synthesised terminal fires `ros2_bridge_task_late_result` instead; `kind: motion` results update `last_result`, control and query results update only the event entity and the bus event.

## Command state machine (`commands.py`)

`created -> sent -> (running | rejected | timeout_no_ack) -> (succeeded | cancelled | aborted | timeout_no_result | lost)`, plus `timeout_no_ack -> running` on a late accepted ack, `sent -> terminal` on a result, and for cancels `sent -> done | rejected | timeout_no_ack`. Terminal exactly once; `late_result` is the only post-terminal signal. The ack timer starts when `async_publish` returns (PUBACK received, or HA's own 10 s ACK timeout logged); the result deadline is `sent_at + effective timeout_s + result_timeout_margin_s`, suspended while paused. `no_ack` is documented as "outcome unknown", not failure. Publishing: build the payload, `await store.async_save()`, `await mqtt.async_publish(..., qos=1, retain=False, message_expiry_interval=ceil(max_age_ms/1000))`; a `ServiceValidationError` from a non-v5 session is retried once without expiry and opens `mqtt_v5_required`; a `HomeAssistantError` (for example `mqtt_broker_error` when HA's client is disconnected) is surfaced as `publish_failed` but the command stays `sent` with the normal ack timeout, because paho keeps the QoS 1 message and resends it on reconnect (verified).

`async_remove_config_entry_device` returns True only when the robot is `offline` or unknown; removal publishes empty retained payloads to `announce`, `state` and `availability` (the echoed tombstone is a no-op).

## Entities per robot (`_attr_has_entity_name = True`, no polling, `PARALLEL_UPDATES = 0`; `Ros2BridgeEntity` implements `async_added_to_hass`, `async_will_remove_from_hass` and `async_entity_id_changed(old_entity_id)` calling `super()`, opting in to in-place entity_id renames now)

| Entity | Platform | unique_id | Details |
|---|---|---|---|
| state (main feature) | sensor | `{robot_id}_state` | ENUM `idle, busy, error`; attributes `task_id, task, since, paused, inhibited, ha_link, watchdog_mode, executor_health, error_code, error_reason, session, instance, progress, stage, message`; `_unrecorded_attributes = frozenset({"progress", "stage", "message", "since", "session"})` |
| last_result | sensor | `{robot_id}_last_result` | ENUM `succeeded, cancelled, aborted, rejected, timeout, lost`; motion tasks only; attributes `task_id, task, code, reason, data, finished_at, duration_ms, synthetic` |
| problem | binary_sensor | `{robot_id}_problem` | PROBLEM; on when `error`, executor health `error`, heartbeat stale while `online`, or `duplicate_robot_id` open; attribute `reasons` |
| task_result | event | `{robot_id}_task_result` | `event_types=[succeeded, cancelled, aborted, rejected, timeout, lost]`, attributes include `kind` |
| one per parameterless task | button | `{robot_id}_task_{task}` | press sends with `source.kind="button"`, `wait="ack"`; rejection raises `task_rejected` |
| cancel | button | `{robot_id}_cancel` | cancels the active task |

risks: Broker authorisation gap: the stock Mosquitto add-on 7.1.1 does not enforce topic ACLs (open issue #4571, not tested on the live add-on), so any authenticated client can publish to ros2_bridge/+/cmd. Mitigations: UUID id check before any reply, allowlist, freshness, persisted dedupe, Retain As Published drop and the optional topic-bound HMAC (off by default per Q15). Stated plainly in docs/security.md.

Probatio dependency: the HA half imports probatio directly because voluptuous is no longer installed at 2026.10.1 (verified). Probatio is a young library (0.13.0) with its own release cadence; API or error-wording changes land with HA monthly releases and Dependabot's harness bump is the trip-wire. Whether probatio ships inline type hints acceptable to mypy strict is inferred from core running mypy strict on it, not verified directly (UNVERIFIED).

Partial application of one objection: the config flow refuses the literal discovery prefix homeassistant plus wildcard and slash forms, but does not read the MQTT integration's configured discovery prefix because that requires mqtt-internal hass.data access with no public helper; a user who changed the discovery prefix and then chose it as the bridge prefix is not protected. Documented and on the post-release track.

Duplicate robot id detection is heuristic on the HA side (differing instance within one heartbeat interval, or more than 3 session changes in 5 minutes): a legitimately crash-looping node also trips it, which is acceptable because both deserve attention, but the repair text must say so. The node-side 0x8E exit depends on the broker sending the reason code; Mosquitto 2.1.2 does, other brokers UNVERIFIED.

Re-adoption after an HA restart depends on the retained state topic and the per-command session in the Store; if the node restarted and finished the task under a new session while HA was down, the result is still applied by id (session no longer filters replies), but a task started under the old session and still running under the new one is impossible by construction, so lost(node_restarted) is correct. A result that was retained and expired (300 s) before HA came back is reported as timeout or lost; reply.result_expiry_s is a parameter.

The persisted dedupe file protects only against publisher-side QoS 1 resends within max_age_cap_ms plus skew; it is written at most once per second, so a crash within that second after an accept leaves a window of one resend. Judged acceptable because the freshness check also applies; documented in failure-modes.md.

Clock dependency: freshness needs both machines on NTP within command.clock_skew_tolerance_ms (2 s). Diagnosable through clock_skew_ms, the clock_skew repair, ha_clock_offset_ms and tools/clock_check.py; Docker Desktop WSL2 clock drift after host sleep is UNVERIFIED and is why e2e step 0 exists.

paho-mqtt 2.1.0 must come from pip (Ubuntu 24.04 apt ships 1.6.1); whether rosdep's pip installer clears PEP 668 on 24.04 without PIP_BREAK_SYSTEM_PACKAGES=1 is UNVERIFIED. The node checks the version at import.

A plugin that blocks indefinitely inside start() or cancel() stalls that robot's node (recorded decision: no thread-pool guard). Consequences are bounded: HA records no_ack (outcome unknown), the heartbeat stops, problem turns on within about 6 s and entities go unavailable after 30 s; other robots are separate processes.

Explicit thread-safety of paho Client.publish() from a non-network thread was not found in the 2.1.0 source (UNVERIFIED); publishes are issued only from the rclpy main thread, which is paho's own README pattern.

The ack timer now starts when async_publish returns; HA's client waits up to 10 s for a PUBACK and then only logs (verified), so a wait: ack caller can block for up to 10 s plus ack_timeout_s on a sick connection. Preferred over timing from issued_at, which produced false no_ack outcomes.

ament_copyright is dropped rather than satisfied: carrying both a full Apache notice and an SPDX line in every ROS source file was judged needless duplication given Q18's SPDX decision; check_spdx.py is the single header gate. If Jonny prefers the ament gate, the phase 0 question (a) is where to say so.

ament_flake8 and ruff could still disagree on a rule outside Q000 and import order (for example flake8-builtins or flake8-comprehensions codes that ruff is not configured to enforce); CI will show it on the first ROS commit and the .flake8 file is the place to reconcile. That flake8-quotes defaults to single quotes remains UNVERIFIED but is moot once Q000 is ignored.

MQTT 5 message expiry on retained replies and Retain As Published are relied on; Mosquitto 2.1.2 honours both. An MQTT 3.1.1-only broker would keep replies for ever and deliver live retained commands with RETAIN 0 (then caught only by freshness and the reconnect-time drop). HA's own client already requires v5.
One active motion task per robot with rejected_busy (no queueing) matches Q17; rapid automations see rejections; queueing is on the post-release track.
Pause semantics (busy with paused true, result pending, both clocks frozen) are defined here because Q7 names pause and resume; what pause means physically is the executor's responsibility.
Latency targets remain provisional (Q8); Zigbee2MQTT payloads carry no source timestamp unless last_seen is enabled (option name UNVERIFIED); phase 5 measures before anything depends on the numbers.
HA test tooling needs Python 3.14.2 or newer and runs in a container or WSL2; whether the pinned harness installs cleanly in python:3.14-slim is a day-one check.
Manifest mqtt discovery is fixed to ros2_bridge/+/announce; users on another prefix set up through the user step. Documented.
Dynamic task buttons: renaming a task removes the old button and breaks dashboards referencing it; task names are an adopter's public contract.
Event entity types are fixed; result codes and kind travel as attributes.
Two HA instances on one broker would both heartbeat and command; instance_id makes it visible in diagnostics but it is not prevented (no origin allowlist in the record).
Executors may misreport status (for example succeeded after a cancel); handles are idempotent and thread-safe but the bridge cannot detect a wrong status.

Live HA as test bed (Q14): safeguards are in place, but an integration bug can still raise repair issues or log noise on the live system, and the retained ha/sensors topics and the deliberate step 6 retained plant touch the live broker.
MoveIt error-code names in docs/writing-an-executor.md are UNVERIFIED against moveit_msgs at Jazzy until phase 7.

judgements_winners: Design 2: Safety, robustness and failure handling first

Design 1: Simplest thing that fully meets the interview record and can ship first. It has the cleanest and most API-correct HA integration, the simplest and now-verified threading model, and the smallest surface to keep correct across monthly HA releases. Every defect found in it is a local, additive fix inside its architecture, whereas Design 2's soundness comes bundled with a riskier three-thread plus worker-pool executor guard and a surface that will cost more each HA release, and Design 3 carries an authorisation bypass in its HMAC and re-opens Q17. The margin is thin (46 against 45) and depends on the grafts below being applied before phase 3.

Design 3: Adopter experience and long-term maintainability (48), ahead of Design 1 (47) and Design 2 (44). It is the only one a ROS team can install with rosdep on Jazzy as written and carry to Lyrical unchanged, and the only one with repairs, troubleshooting, a template executor and a monthly HA-release routine. Its safety gaps (payload-only HMAC, no executor guard, no ROS to HA heartbeat) are grafts from Design 2, not reasons to prefer it.
